why: Task 514 loaded 30,897,557 rows and 11,273,954 of them (36.5%) reached the
collection with no `trust_tier` and no `source_type`; 19,619,656 (63.5%),
including the whole 19.2M Wikipedia slice, carried no BM25 posting at all.
Every count check passed, because conservation counts ROWS and not what is
in them. Task 516's fedlex defect is the same class one level down: 22,928
titles that were present, non-empty, and did not contain the handle the
query uses.
So the build now declares what a shipped payload must LOOK like, per set and
per family, and refuses a stage that does not meet it. A threshold here is a
judgement about how much of the collection may be unrankable; it is data, it
has a `why`, and moving it is a visible diff.
evaluated_by: measures the same fields as is_empty on the built collection)

why: 0.5% missing a serving signal is task 515's declared allowance, measured at
0.4066%. 0.1% with no posting is two orders of magnitude tighter than what
task 514 shipped and one order looser than what task 515/516 measure
(13 rows, 0.00004%): a genuinely textless point is legal, a slice of them
is not.
0.5% with a provenance head is the same allowance applied to the defect
class task 516 and task 517 each found once: a materializer that writes its
own bookkeeping into the head of the document, where the chunker turns it
into the snippet AND the head of the dense embedding. fedlex shipped
22,913 of 22,928 like that; context7 shipped 72,330 of 126,427. Neither was
visible to any count check, because the row is present, titled or not, and
conservation balances either way.

wikipedia_413a.why: 19,227,106 in-place re-embeds whose posting is CARRIED from the twin by point id. A single row without one means the carry failed, and 63.5% of task 514's collection is what that looks like when nobody counts it.

task477_direct_capture_epoch4_chunks.measured: 2,301 of 224,439 staged rows (1.0252%) carry no title
why: NOT a regression, and measured on both sides rather than asserted. All
2,301 rows are github.com blob URLs, all 2,301 are PRESENT in the sealed
membership of the collection this build replaces, and production's title
for every one of them is null: 2,301 of 2,301 `url_present_title_null`,
0 `url_present_title_present`, 0 absent from the registry
(, measured 2026-09-05 against
serving-metadata-registry.v2.sqlite through `aw_serving_metadata.url_key`
so the key is the projection's own, not a re-implementation).
The 0.5% default is a BUILD-WIDE allowance carried down to the unit; a
per-set ceiling that matches what production itself ships is calibration,
not a waiver. The number to watch is the direction: if this set ever
titles FEWER rows than production does, the default is not what catches
it -- a rate with no counterpart never was the measurement (task 516 §3).

rfc-editor-production-current-v2.status: KNOWN DEFECT, NOT FIXED -- this ceiling is the measured rate, set so the task-517 build could proceed. It is a waiver in substance and it is on Tim's decision list ( section 9).
why: The SAME defect class as fedlex and context7, in a
third family, found only because task 517 generalized the pattern from the
four github `aw_*` keys to any of them: `restage_rfc_editor_markdown.py` (now `cytir/extract/rfc_editor.py restage`, task 1261)
opens every RFC with `--- aw_rfc_number: N / aw_source_path / ... ---`,
and the chunker's section-adjacent policy makes that block the head of
chunk 0 -- the snippet AND the head of the dense embedding.
It is a REGRESSION, not parity: 0 of a 200-row sample of the collection
this build replaces (aw_e3, domain rfc-editor.org) opens with the block,
against an expected ~20 if the rates matched.
The producer is FIXED for future runs (pipeline, task 517); this build's
44,543 rows were not re-materialized because doing so needs the family's
own chain re-run and the task's remaining budget was owed to the gate
separation.
rfc-editor-production-current-v2.unparks_when: the rfc-editor family is re-materialized without the front matter; then this entry is deleted and the default 0.5% applies.

fedlex-r0-exact-current-v1.sample: Obligationenrecht (OR; SR 220) — Art. 411 — IV. Kreditnehmer und Auftraggeber
why: Swiss federal law is searched for by its SR number and its abbreviation,
not by its formal docTitle: every legal gold the 1024 build lost is
abbreviation-led (URG, DSG, StPO, ZGB, CO, LCR, LTVA). The collection this
build replaces carries an SR number on 23,495 of its 23,872 fedlex rows
(98.4%); the epoch-4 re-materialization carried it on 0 of 22,928 and
nothing refused. 95% is below production's own rate, so this fails only on
a real regression, not on the 118 articles production itself titles with
the bare docTitle.

_absent_family.note: A family with no entry here is NOT checked. Adding one is how a family's title contract becomes checkable; inventing a pattern for a family whose production titles never had one would fail a build over a rule nobody measured a need for (task 516 section 3: jorf, kali, cantonal, gesetze and legifrance production titles carry no SR number at all).

why: Task 535 sec.3.1: the collection this build replaces carries `published`
on 4,969,090 of its pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov rows against ADR-090's own
count of 4,969,092 single-unit no-op documents for this family -- i.e.
effectively every pubmed row twin-side. Task 536 found the mechanism:
`published` was never in `aw_serving_metadata.REGISTRY_FIELDS`, so the
sealed pubmed stage record (identity + text, no serving payload) had
nowhere to recover it from and this build shipped 27,839 of 5,208,018,
0 of them pubmed. 99% (not 100%) leaves headroom for the sample of
pubmed's own production rows that never had a `published` date at all
(a `<PubDate>` XML field with no year, historically a small residue),
same margin style as the fedlex title-shape entry above.

_absent_family.note: OPT-IN, same posture as title_shape: a family with no entry here is not checked for `published` presence. ADR-039's shared payload_minimum has no `published` field in it for ANY of the 86 declared families (task 535 sec.3.5), so declaring one here for a family that never stamped it in production would fail a build over a rule nobody measured a need for. Add an entry only once the twin's own rate for that family is measured (task 535 sec.3.1's per-domain table names iris.who.int, finma.ch and the Swiss news domains as the other candidates).

_why: ONE stored body serving MANY distinct URLs. Invisible to every count
check (the rows are all present, conservation balances) and to the
provenance-head rule (the text is a real fragment of a real page, just
the same wrong fragment for every page): the task-517 contract flagged
5 of 127,074 task472_f2_html rows while 17,850 of them were collapsed.
MEASURED (task 521 / 523). Pre-fix, on the staged payloads the build
actually loads: 21 cohorts of >= 25 distinct URLs, 7,985 of 127,074
rows = 6.28%, sparse postings 27..205 -- eeoc.gov 3,010 URLs at 34
postings (the '.gov websites use HTTPS' banner), edudoc.ch 1,082 at 27,
has-sante.fr 1,970 at 205.
ROOT CAUSE and fix: libxml2 mis-nested <main> into <nav> on malformed
USWDS markup, trafilatura's boilerplate prune then deleted the page, and
recover_wild_text salvaged the banner. aw_common now re-parses such a
document through the stdlib HTML parser. Post-fix the same lane measures
edudoc.ch 1,082 -> 0.
THE CEILING IS PER LANE AND OPT-IN. N and the posting ceiling are
judgements about a lane's own content shape; a number nobody measured
for a lane must not decide whether that lane ships. Two lanes are
measured and NOT yet declared, because their residue has not been
decomposed: task472_cc_materializer_1024_embed 236 cohorts / 50,046 of
621,975 rows (8.05%) and task477_direct_capture_epoch4_chunks 134
cohorts / 137,281 of 349,798 rows (39.25%), the latter dominated by
eur-lex documents of 1,000+ tokens that the posting ceiling excludes.

why: N=25: the measured distribution has no cohort between 25 and 27, so
the cut is in a gap and not on a slope.
256 postings: the whole pre-fix cohort head sits at 27..205, and the
eur-lex duplicates that are genuine shared DOCUMENTS (one text at
many language URLs, 1,000+ dense tokens) sit far above it. The unit
is distinct BM25 postings because the stored snippet is truncated to
25 words and cannot tell a 72-token banner from a 700-token page.
3%: the post-fix lane measures 2.44% (4,098 of 168,128 rows), and
1,970 of those rows are has-sante.fr -- NOT an extraction defect but
the origin serving one document at many nested-path URLs (four
sampled captures, four identical <title>s, extraction correct on
all four). The pre-fix lane measured 6.28% and this ceiling REFUSES
it, which is the point. The number to watch is the direction: this
residue should fall as the capture-side duplicates are fixed, and a
rise means a new extractor defect, not a new corpus.

_why: Task 535: the epoch-4 generic packer cut long, densely-sectioned reference
documents at a 3.73x lower chunk count than the collection production serves
-- 82 hosts, ~1.01M rows down, 150 of the 262 golds lost on the held-out
1,418 set -- and nothing in the repo could see it. Two reasons, both closed
here. (1) No row could state its own width: the chunker computed
`chunk_n_words` and `project_record` discarded it, so 535 had to argue the
question from a chunk-COUNT ratio and record merged-vs-dropped as
unmeasurable (535 sec.2.3). Task 536 landed the passthrough. (2) No family
had ever been asked which policy it cuts with: 84 of 86 declare
chunk_policy.policy_id 'unknown'.
THE ARMS.
policy_sha256                the bytes of the policy the set declares. A
policy is identified by its hash; a different
hash is a different rule, not a renamed one.
min_chunk_n_words_presence   a row that cannot state its own width cannot
be checked at all.
max_rows_over_hard_max_frac  rows wider than the declared policy's own
word_guard.hard_max. A STRUCTURAL invariant of
the chunker, not a tuned threshold: 0.0 is the
only honest value, because a row above the
guard was not cut by the policy the set names.
max_mis_selected_frac        OPTIONAL fourth arm. The share of rows whose
page the ratified selector
(data/chunk-reference-selector.v1.json)
assigns to a DIFFERENT policy family than the
one the row was cut under. This is the arm
that catches task 535's actual defect, in
which every row was correctly declared epoch-4
and the PAGES were in the wrong family. It
needs the materializer to stamp
`chunk_selector` (it holds the markdown; the
payload stage does not), so declaring it for a
lane that does not stamp is a FAIL,
deliberately -- not a skip.
OPT-IN PER SET, same posture as title_shape, published_presence and
extraction_collapse. A route with no markdown page -- source-native records,
entity cards, preserved passages (chunk.atomic / chunk.preserved in
data/chunk-policy-registry.v1.json) -- has no width to declare, and no set
already in aw_e8 is declared here: their stage trees were sealed before the
task-536 passthrough existed, so a presence floor would fail a build over
evidence that cannot be re-created without re-staging. The sets that would
backfill onto them are named in specs/chunk-reference-epoch.md.

why: The chunk.reference delta's own set id. Every threshold is 0 or 1
because this lane is NEW: it is produced by
materialize, which runs the chunker
under the pinned policy and stamps chunk_n_words and chunk_selector on
every row it writes. There is no historical residue to tolerate and
therefore no margin to invent; a margin here would be a tolerance for a
defect nobody has measured (memory: cold-read-specs-and-circular-filters,
round numbers are the tell).
The entry is live before the lane exists on purpose: evaluate() only sees
set ids the stage actually produced, so this binds the day the delta
stages and changes nothing before then.

_absent_set.note: OPT-IN. A set with no entry here is not checked for chunk width. Adding one for a set already sealed in aw_e8 requires re-staging it, because the presence of chunk_n_words on a staged record is a property of the run that produced it (task 536 sec.2.1) and cannot be backfilled onto a sealed stage tree.
